candidates.title: [Feature] Reduce redundant tokenizer initialization during startup
candidates.snippet: ### Motivation  Startup loads the same text tokenizer in both `Scheduler` and `TpModelWorker` within one process. `_fix_v5_tokenizer_components` also rebuilds the full vocabulary just to inspect the pre-tokenizer and decoder.  Reusing the scheduler's tokenizer and loading only those two components can make startup a little faster, including server restarts. A local Qwen3-32B-FP8 check reduced the component-loading step from about 240 ms to 18 ms.

candidates.title: mlxrunner: Qwen3 runtime ignores YaRN rope scaling
candidates.snippet: ### What is the issue?  The MLX runner's Qwen3 runtime (`Qwen3ForCausalLM`) reads only `rope_theta` from config.json and ignores `rope_scaling`, so checkpoints that configure YaRN run with plain RoPE. YaRN also scales queries and keys by its mscale (about 1.139 at factor 4) at every sequence length, so these models' outputs drift from mlx-lm and transformers even on short prompts, not only past the original context.  Affected checkpoints set `rope_scaling` with `"rope_type": "yarn"`, for example

candidates.title: mlxrunner: fused linear-attention kernels skip float16 activations
candidates.snippet: ### What is the issue?  Two fused kernels run in every linear-attention layer of Qwen 3.5, Qwen3-Next and qwen4_exp: the causal conv with SiLU, then the gated delta. Both are generic over the input dtype, but their dispatch accepts only bfloat16 (the conv also takes float32). A checkpoint whose activations run in float16 takes the slower graph implementation of both in every one of those layers. The conv kernel also serves Nemotron-H's Mamba layers.
